text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Telemalta to spend $9 million in upgrading communications, A main advantage of the upgrade is that it would enable quick tracing of malicious, anonymous calls.

- Prime Minister Alfred Sant says three White Papers to be issued on armed forces, covering their effectiveness, the setting up of a reserve corps and setting up a soldiers' association. Sant, speaking as Maltese soldiers took part in a joint exercise with Italian and Greek soldiers in Sicily, said that although Malta had withdrawn from the Partnership for Peace programme, Maltese soldiers would continue to take part in overseas exercises as long as Maltese neutrality was not violated. Maltese soldiers would also continue to be trained in the United States, Britain, Italy and Germany.
- New dockyard chairman encountering resistance to reform.

- Workers find more catacombs at Rabat, nine miles north of Valletta. Rabat, one of Malta's oldest towns, is honeycombed by ancient catacombs dug hundreds of years ago as burial places and places of worship by early Christians when Malta was ruled by the Arabs.

- Education Minister Evarist Bartolo tells teachers conference that ministry would seek ways to encourage more young people to teach in primary schools where there is a shortage of teachers. Action would also be taken to revise curricula to ease stress on students, and a crackdown would be made on bullying, he said.
- Man dies after falling off horse.
- Action planned by the government to increase effectiveness of the law courts and reduce the backlog of cases, which runs into thousands.
